verdict_rationale: The kernel check and the token metric are sound, deterministic and shipped to the agent byte for byte. But the reference checker cannot run in the agent sandbox, the self-check runs no Lean, the public examples' allowed use contradicts the prompt, and the score has no measured floor. A model-free tactic search scores 27 with no spend, so the task measures Lean search engineering more than ML or budget use.
floor: There is no normalization. task.yaml has no score_normalization block, so the reward is 100 x the raw mean reduction. 0 = the unchanged proof, which is what failed requests and the smoke fixture return (validate.py:43-47, solution/server.py:80-81). That is the natural floor, but it is not a calibrated baseline. The data build drops only statements that one fixed `first | omega | rfl | ... | exact?` closer solves (pipeline/build_data.py:27-28, 128-129). Cheap closers such as `bound` still solve many items (Opus 1g91nm: 183 of 700 dev problems), and a model-free search scored 27.0 at $0.25 (DeepSeek teia0r). So a trivial non-ML baseline sits far above 0.
ceiling: 100 is unreachable: an empty proof scores 0 (simplification_metric.py:130), so the best possible per item is 1 - 1/original_tokens. The ceiling is not binding. The best observed score is 40.5.
feasible_at_10: yes: Opus scored 33.9 at $10. A model-free search scored 27 with almost no spend (DeepSeek teia0r $0.25, 417mxo $0). An off-the-shelf 7B prover served with vLLM fits on the grading H100 at no wallet cost.
budget_scaling: None. The 19-model mean falls slightly (15.8 / 15.4 / 14.6), and the top-6 gain from $10 to $200 is about 2 points (sensitivity.md:135). Most of the work is CPU-side Lean search at inference, which runs on the grader's H100 box and 8 CPUs for free. Opus's $200 run (40.5) is the only high-wallet gain larger than 2 SE.
selfcheck_fidelity: Partial. The self-check launches the server as grading does and sends 7 windows of 8 public proofs through grading's own collect_predictions, with the same 60 s window and the first window cold (verifier.py:131-195). That is good fidelity for the latency gate (7 of grading's 45 windows). But no proof is checked by Lean (verifier.py:161-162). The CONTRACT tells agents to run the reference checker in /artifacts/lean-checker (CONTRACT.md:15), but that checker needs Docker (checker/README.md:37, 59), and the sandbox has none ('docker: not found', Muse 3gdrrt). Agents had to clone the checker themselves. A submission can pass the self-check and still return proofs the official checker rejects: three trials did (valid_fraction 0.90-0.99), and Muse 138qky measured 0.115 on its own checker but scored 0.0325.
judge: No LLM judge in the metric: validity comes from the Lean 4.15.0 kernel, through an environment replay and an axiom whitelist (tests/task/checker/ProofCheck.lean:27-59), and length from a deterministic lexer. The reviewer (Claude Opus 5.5, global) applies three checks: provenance, no proof lookup and the actual inference path (tests/task/review.py:12-42).
neutrality: No vendor-specific element. The lexer is model-agnostic. The only organizer feasibility probe was an API run of GPT-6 Astra, one of the evaluated models (pipeline/validation_results.json:27-38), but it does not enter grading. The input proofs were generated by open provers, and the top runs used the same families (DeepSeek-Prover-V2, Goedel-Prover), which every harness can download. The score rewards knowledge of Lean tactics (`bound`, `nlinarith` hint pruning) about as much as ML skill.
reference_solution: solution/ is the shared smoke fixture. Its /simplify handler returns the input proof unchanged (solution/server.py:80-81), which scores exactly 0. The fixture's README says it 'cannot pass architecture gates'. The organizer's only score is a GPT-6 Astra API probe, 0.243 on the 55 public proofs, which is not an offline submission. validation_results.json:14-18 marks the task 'release_ready': false, with 'No current-best permitted baseline or $50 improvement pilot'. Solvability is shown only by the trials.

issues.finding: The CONTRACT tells agents to run the shipped reference Lean checker to get a score, but that checker needs Docker, which the agent sandbox lacks, and its README says not to run it in the candidate sandbox. The self-check runs no Lean either. Agents therefore never get an official validity check before grading, and each one has to rebuild a checker that matches the grader's options (maxRecDepth 1024, the `open` line, 1 CPU, 4 GiB, a 60 s wall clock).

issues.affects: Every model. It hurts most the agents whose home-made checkers drift from the official one: Muse 3gdrrt had 10% invalid proofs, and Muse 138qky measured 0.115 against a held-out 0.0325.

issues.finding: The prompt and CONTRACT forbid selecting on 'the validation or test split of any public dataset or benchmark', and nothing tells the agent where the 55 public examples come from. The reviewer explicitly allows tuning on them. The pipeline draws public examples from the organizer's 'validation' statements, which in the shared Lean pipeline are half miniF2F-test (see the next issue). lean-validity states this exception in its CONTRACT; lean-simplification does not. Cautious agents (Opus, Gemini) avoided tuning on validation.jsonl, while others tuned on it openly.

issues.affects: Rule-cautious agents (Opus, Gemini) lose a tuning signal that others (Fable vb4un4, DeepSeek teia0r, Muse 3gdrrt) used. The effect is small next to the 1.5-point SE, but its direction is against careful agents.

issues.finding: The held-out set is probably not drawn like the public set. build_data.py reads a source run whose files and schema match the lean-validity pipeline: statements.jsonl with sid/split, originals.jsonl, check1_originals.jsonl, the same HEADER and the same four upstream pools. It sends upstream 'validation' statements to public and 'heldout' plus organizer 'train' statements to private. In that pipeline, validation is 50% miniF2F-test, 25% Lean Workbook and 25% Goedel-Pset, all verbatim, while held-out and train are numeric or renamed variants of Workbook (45%), Pset (45%) and FormalMATH (10%). If so, the held-out set has no miniF2F statements. That would correct the existing note's finding 3, which says the held-out set draws on miniF2F-test. It would also mean a distribution shift between the public and held-out sets. The data were built by 2026-09-24, before lean-validity's 2026-09-26 fix that removed held-out statements found verbatim in public pools (26% of them). lean-simplification's build has no verbatim-public audit, only a structural family dedup against public, so some held-out theorems may appear verbatim in Lean Workbook, whose public proof corpora are allowed training data.

issues.affects: Every model equally for the shift. Verbatim overlap would favour agents that trained or built dev pools on Lean-workbook-proofs (Opus 348kgu and 1g91nm, Gemini, Astra 4d7hxi) in a small, unmeasured way. A lookup would still be caught by no_proof_lookup.

issues.finding: There are no measured anchors. The reward is the raw reduction, the unchanged-proof zero is the only floor, and no organizer baseline was run under the submission rules. A model-free tactic portfolio reaches about 27, so roughly two thirds of the observed range comes from Lean search with no ML, and wallet size does not move the score.
evidence: tasks/lean-simplification/tests/task/pipeline/validation_results.json:14-17 '"release_ready": false ... No current-best permitted baseline or $50 improvement pilot has been established.'
issues.affects: This compresses the differences between models. Strong agents that build ML pipelines gain few points over a pure-search agent such as DeepSeek (27 at $0).

issues.finding: The gate is all-or-nothing: one batch of 8 over 60 s fails the whole run. Search servers are anytime and wall-clock bound, so both their output and their deadline risk depend on the grading box's CPU speed. The self-check measures 7 of the 45 windows, the first one cold, which covers this well. No trial lost its run this way.

issues.finding: Lexer quirk: a dot-qualified chain is one token (`h.1.le.trans` counts as 1), so projection and dot-notation chains are cheaper than the equivalent applications. This is documented in the shipped metric file and the same for everyone.
issues.affects: Neutral. It rewards agents that read the metric code.
